2H26 獲利展望平淡 
重要訊息 
儒鴻舉行法說會。受到中東戰事與通膨再起影響，除客戶對4Q26 訂單趨於
保守外，管理層對原物料價格波動影響之看法比3 月法說會更加謹慎。 
評論及分析 
致力新品開發與導入。隨著訂單能見度保持約六個月，儒鴻看到在中東戰事
不確定性與美國通膨再起之環境下，客戶對4Q26 訂單持保守態度。管理層
維持每月營收30 億元目標，隱含2026 年營收成長將較平淡，對比前四月
為年增1%。公司將持續關注美國消費者習慣改變與客戶動向，並全力推動
客戶採用新產品，目前新品營收佔比約15-20%。 
原物料價格波動。為因應原物料價格劇烈波動，公司採取措施包括建立低價
庫存、與上游廠商洽談長期協議，並將在未來價格會議中轉嫁予客戶。公司
表示，在當前外部環境動盪中，2026 年毛利率展望保持28-32%已可視為
營運實力之展現。儘管紡織原物料斷料風險極低，管理層對原物料價格波動
潛在影響之看法明顯比3 月法說會更加謹慎。 
2H26 獲利成長展望受限。1Q26 獲利年增9%、季增16%至18.4 億元，或
每股盈餘6.69 元，高於預期係因利潤率超前。儘管1Q26 營收成長有限，
年增3%、季增4%至96.2 億元，高毛利新品銷售佔比提升趨動毛利率回升
至32.2%，為過去六季以來新高。我們大致維持2026 年每股盈餘預估，為
年增22%至24.44 元。考量2Q25 為匯率波動導致之低基期，我們預計
2Q26 每股盈餘將強勁年增183%至6.20 元，但3Q-4Q26 每股盈餘將分別
收縮至5.97、5.59 元，年減1%、3%。 
投資建議 
反映1Q26 財報超前，凱基微幅上調目標價至367 元，係基於2026 年每股
盈餘預估之15 倍不變推算得出。考量中東戰事對訂單與利潤率影響將落後
於2H26 顯現，我們維持「持有」評等。 
投資風險 
訂單復甦較預期強勁、原物料價格與匯率變動。

能源消耗 
直接與間接能源消耗總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司運營範圍內消耗之能源總量 
- 能源使用總量 = 直接能源消耗總量 + 間接能源消耗量 
- 總能源使用量包括購買的能源、生產的能源 
- 就公用事業而言，輸電/電網損耗為其業務活動之一部分，被視為總能源消耗，數據不包括
為滿足能源使用而生產的電力（公用事業為出售而生產） 
- 就公用事業而言，用於能源生產的煤、天然氣或核能等原料不屬於「總能源使用」項下 
 
購買之再生能源 
再生能源購買總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司各種來源之能源消耗量與購買的能源中屬於自然界可再生者（太陽能、風能、水能、
生物質能、地熱能）之量  
- 如無證據顯示再生能源由公司生產，則所報告的能源數據視為購買的再生能源 
 
再生能源使用率 
再生能源占總能源消耗量之比例 
 
約當二氧化碳排放量 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸) 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合
物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
 
單位營收碳排量 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量（公噸）銷售（百萬元）比 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合
物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
 
廢棄物總量 
廢棄物總量(公噸) 
- 總廢棄物 = 無害廢棄物 + 有害廢棄物 
- 僅考慮固體廢棄物，但如液體廢棄物以公噸為單位呈報，則會將其加入求得包含液體廢棄
物之總量 
- 對於採礦、石油與天然氣等行業，tailings、廢石、煤、飛灰等廢棄物亦考慮在內 
 
廢棄物回收比例 
公司呈報的廢棄物回收比例 
- 廢棄物回收比例 = 廢棄物回收量/總廢棄物*100 
- 廢棄物轉化為能源或經由廢棄物焚燒產生能源視為廢棄物回收 
- 經由堆肥回收的廢棄物視為回收之廢棄物 
 
耗水量 
耗水量(立方公尺) 
- 由呈報組織直接或經水公司等中介機構從任何水源抽取的總水量 
- 水井、城鎮/公用事業/市政用水、河水、地表水等不同之水源均予以考慮 
 
環保支出 
環保支出總金額 
- 所有用於環境保護，或防止、減少、控制環境因素、影響、危害的投資與支出，亦包括處
置、處理、衛生、清理支出 
 
員工流動率 
員工流動率 
- 包括任何原因（自願或非自願）離開公司的員工，如辭職、退休、自然離職/死亡、醫療失
能、冗員、裁員、重組、解僱、裁減或定期合約到期 
- 員工流動率 =（離開之員工/平均員工人數）*100 
- 平均員工人數 =（本年末員工人數 + 去年末員工人數）/2 
- 本財年末員工數 =上個財年末員工數 + 新員工數 - 離開之員工數

- 女性主管百分比 = 女性主管人數/主管總數*100

最大客戶網通機櫃訂單除由美國擴展至歐亞，產品更延伸至AI 機櫃，

神達全力擴產支應網通及AI 機櫃強勁成長，且業外豐富轉投資，每年

重點更新

率升值幅度有限，雖礙於產能滿載，營收估小幅季增2%，然預期營益率將有

營收季增幅擴大至雙位數，今、明年EPS 將跳升至5、8.3 元水準。 
高速成長期才剛開始，神雲營益率由去年1.3%至1H25 大幅跳升至近6%

大型CSP 資料中心通常約配置1,500~2,000 個伺服器機櫃，雖伺服器機櫃中配置交換器於機櫃頂端，然大型資料
中心通常會在額外於資料中心設置網通機櫃以利管理網路，過往在通用伺服器為主體的資料中心，伺服器機櫃搭配
網通機櫃的相對配比較低，推估僅約低至中個位數水準，估一個資料中心若有千個伺服器機櫃，僅需配置數十個網
通機櫃即可因應高速網路傳輸。然在AI 浪潮崛起後，AI 伺服器資料中心呈現高密度的配置，預期高階AI 伺服器搭
配網通機櫃的比重將拉升數倍，以反映AI 伺服器更高密度的網路需求。

光通訊金凸塊替營運帶來質變，獲利步入新擴張期 
重要訊息 
凱基更新對頎邦營運近況的觀點，並納入2026-28 年財測。我們認為公司在
光通訊業務的發展正迎來結構性的技術轉折，並將伴隨強勁的需求爆發。 
評論及分析 
光通訊業務迎來結構性的技術轉折。隨著光收發模組架構逐步朝200G/lane
推進，單一通道速率的提升對訊號品質、雜訊容忍度及傳輸距離的要求日益
嚴苛。若在200G/lane 速率下仍沿用傳統打線封裝進行光電訊號的傳輸與轉
換，過長的訊號路徑將導致嚴重的雜訊與訊號衰減。為確保訊號完整性，能
有效縮短電訊號路徑的金凸塊技術已成為不可或缺的解決方案。金凸塊憑藉
導電性佳、延展性好、低雜訊及高可靠性等優勢，在高速光通訊領域受青
睞。目前頎邦在光通訊晶片金凸塊領域已有逾10 個專案同步推進，其中進
度最明確的主力產品TIA 晶片已於1Q26 順利進入量產。在客戶佈局上，既
有量產客戶之訂單能見度有望延伸至2028 年，預期其他客戶產品也將陸續
通過驗證。我們看好光通訊晶片金凸塊業務於2027 年具備至少翻倍成長的
潛力，並將於2028 年延續翻倍成長的強勁動能。高毛利的新業務不僅將推
升公司整體獲利水準，在200G/lane 光收發模組強勁的需求支撐下，我們對
頎邦後續的出貨量能與獲利擴張保持樂觀。預估光通訊晶片金凸塊業務將佔
今年總營收4-6%，並於2027-28 年分別攀升至10-12%與20-22%。 
既有營運基礎具抵禦性利多。儘管市場對消費性電子需求下滑存有疑慮，但
DDI 與RF 元件作為頎邦重要的營運基石，其抵禦性因子將有效化解相關風
險。首先，公司已成功向客戶實施漲價策略以穩固獲利；其次，隨著韓國同
業逐步退出8 吋相關產能並轉向高毛利業務，代工需求預期將流向台廠，頎
邦可望順利承接外溢的訂單增量，為營收挹注正面動能。此外，佔頎邦營收
約30%的美系智慧型手機客戶，其對DDI 與RF 元件的需求維持穩健，該客
戶市佔率的增長將抵銷中低階Android 機種需求疲弱所帶來的不利影響。 
投資建議 
綜合上述光通訊晶片金凸塊業務的強勁成長引擎，以及既有DDI 與RF 元件
業務的防禦性優勢，我們看好頎邦將於2026-28 年步入新一輪的獲利成長軌
道，預估此三年的EPS 將分別年增41.4%、40.8%與25.8%，達5.30 元、
7.45 元與9.38 元。考量光通訊業務迎來結構性技術轉折與需求爆發、既有
DDI 業務受惠漲價策略使ASP 有撐，加上長期將受惠於韓國同業退出成熟代
工業務的板塊轉移效應，我們預期公司估值將迎來re-rating 的契機。據
此，我們重啟並給予頎邦「增加持股」評等，並以2028 年預估EPS 之30
倍作為估值基礎，換算目標價為280 元。 
投資風險 
光通訊驗證與擴產延宕；消費性電子需求持續疲弱衝擊漲價效益。

長期朝向提供光通訊晶片一站式封測服務。受惠於過往在DDI 業務累積的龐
大產能與設備共用優勢，頎邦在金凸塊製程上並無產能瓶頸。目前產業面臨
的主要挑戰在於AI 晶片需求激增，導致整體封測端切割與測試產能吃緊。
為此，公司的擴產策略將以切割為首要優先，其次為測試，最後方為金凸
塊。頎邦正積極從單一的金凸塊供應商，轉型為涵蓋切割與測試的一站式封
測服務提供者，此舉不僅能大幅縮短生產週期、減少時間浪費，更能深化客
戶黏著度。與此同時，公司正密切與海外設備商接洽，積極強化在光測試領
域的技術經驗與設備佈局。 
在光通訊晶片金凸塊製程市場擁有一定程度的技術護城河。金凸塊製程涉及
複雜的材料配方、參數設定與深厚的現場實務經驗，競爭對手即便購入相同
的硬體設備，仍需至少一至兩年的學習曲線方能追趕。加上頎邦與客戶共同
開發的專利細節具有高度排他性，形成難以輕易複製的技術護城河。展望未
來網通產業趨勢，面對共同封裝光學(CPO)與可插拔光收發模組的技術路線
發展，我們認為可插拔模組憑藉高度的維修彈性，能有效規避CPO 停機成
本過高的痛點，預期兩種技術架構將在未來市場中並存數年。 
2Q26 營運穩健向上。展望2Q26 營運，受惠於產能利用率持續回溫、美系
智慧型手機品牌需求暢旺，加上產品組合進一步優化，我們預估單季營收將
能繳出10-15%的季增長。在獲利能力方面，毛利率預期將季增3.0-3.5 個
百分點，達26.6%。

營運現況 
 
1. 伺服器/資料中心應用方面，GB300 AI伺服器機櫃已於近期放量出
貨，GB300機櫃的Switch Tray之水冷板、快接頭用量較GB200機櫃
有所提升，將挹注公司未來營收成長動能。 
2. 子公司富世達YT3Q25占奇鋐營收9.2%，富世達除供應摺疊手機軸
承，也切入水冷快接頭等AI伺服器零組件應用，表現同樣出色，10
月營收13.1億元，YoY 43.4%，續創單月新高。 
3. 3C應用方面，手機VC部分，今年占整體營收個位數百分比，預期明
年營收占比將提升。  
4. 奇鋐將維持在 NVIDIA 與 ASIC 兩大供應鏈的核心角色，並透過水冷
分歧管 (Manifold) 產品線的份額從明年起顯著擴大至 5-10%，創造
出第二個重要的營收成長動能。Rubin有望導入MCCP成為明年新一
代Vera Rubin散熱解決方案，公司目前協同客戶開發中，看好公司
明年營收及獲利表現將持續向上。 
 
 
 
未來成長動能 
 
1. AI伺服器應用方面(GPU占7成；ASIC占2~3成)，公司看好明年整體
水冷散熱需求強勁，同時也看好ASIC的發展，將是公司未來成長的
一大動能。公司目前已和各大CSP客戶合作這一代及下一代ASIC專
案，同時也與NVIDIA、AMD保持密切合作，目前的ASIC仍以氣冷
方案為主，不過由於目前水冷版本仍在測試中，僅少部分的ASIC採
用水冷散熱。若後續水冷良率提升，則水冷滲透率將進一步提高。
我們預期ASIC AI伺服器未來水冷滲透率將會持續上升。 
2. 我們預估2H26 ASIC有多位客戶新世代水冷板放量，同時公司有望
切入新CSP ASIC水冷板供應。機櫃需求強勁跟降噪機櫃新產品線是
明年另一成長動能。 
3. ASIC 散熱方案由氣冷轉向液冷:目前大多數 ASIC 晶片功耗尚未超過 
1,000W，因此仍主要採用傳統氣冷方案，僅有 AWS Trainium 2.5 
和 Meta MTIA 2 等少數產品開始試行水冷散熱。然而隨著新的資料
中心逐步完成水冷基礎設施的建置，以及未來更高功率晶片的量
產，ASIC 伺服器的水冷滲透率預計將在 2026 年大幅提高。 
4. Trainium 專案詳情： 原本 Trainium 2 採用均熱板 (VC) 氣冷散熱。
從 2025 年第四季量產的 Trainium 2.5 開始，部分機型將導入水冷
散熱，且設計上分為 Compute Tray 和 Switch Tray，每個晶片都將
有獨立的水冷板，並採用 UQD (水冷轉接頭) 進行連接，其採用數量
將明顯高於 GB200/GB300 平台。 
5. 初期挑戰與未來趨勢：雖然 Trainium 3 初期水冷滲透率預計在 20% 
至 30% 之間，但長期來看，對於 Google TPU V6、Meta MTIA 2、
Microsoft Maia 2 和 AWS Trainium 3 等高功率 ASIC 而言，液冷散
熱將成為不可或缺的主流散熱選項。

1Q26 銀行與壽險核心獲利雙位數成長 
重要訊息   
1Q26 金控稅後淨利年增16%，前4 月金控獲利285 億元，年增率上揚至
26%，若加計FVOCI 股票資本利得，則調整後獲利年增76%。  
評論及分析 
銀行、壽險帶動1Q26 獲利年增16%。中信金1Q26 稅後淨利年增、季增
16%至231 億元，主要中信銀提存前獲利年增17%帶動稅後淨利年增23%
至166 億元，加上台壽保稅後淨利年增39%至77.5 億元，其中認列一次性投
資型保單改採IFRS15 重新衡量37 億元。公司表示中信金前4 月稅後淨利若加
計FVOCI 股票資本利得111 億元，則調整後獲利達396 億元，年增76%，
未來配發現金股利則以調整後獲利為基礎。 
1Q26 銀行核心獲利維持成長動能。中信銀1Q26 淨利差季增4 基點至
1.68%，含FX swap 收益則為1.72%，反映1Q26 淨利息收入季增4.2%、
年增23.6%，主要存放比季增1.1%至76.4%、外幣資金成本改善及有價證
券收益提升。公司維持2026F 調整後淨利差為1.7-1.73%，並預估今年央行
升息可能升息共1 碼，提升淨利差1.7 基點，放款成長上修至雙位數成長，
但提升全年信用成本增加3 基點至28-33 基點。1Q26 手續費收入成長
19.7%，其中財管手收成長28%，高於全年低雙位數成長目標。 
1Q26 台壽保淨值回升約250 億元。1Q26 台壽保合約服務邊際(CSM)攤銷
為32.3 億元，年化攤銷率約為7.9%，加上1Q26 銷售新契約CSM 之35.6
億元，1Q26 CSM 餘額上揚至1,720 億元。1Q26 台壽保投報率3.3%(包含
FVOCI 股票資本利得0.22%)，其中避險後經常性收益率約2.54%扣除負債
成本2.44%後之正利差約10 基點。1Q26 其他權益虧損257 億元，其中
1/1 接軌IFRS17 重分類影響135 億元，1Q26 股票未實現損益為215 億元，
4 月上揚至1,000 億元。此外，由於1Q26 台債及美債利率上揚，帶動保險
負債公允價值下降約254 億元，部分抵銷FVOCI 債券虧損影響。 
投資建議

市場熱絡亦將支撐手續費收入高個位數增長，加上台壽保CSM 攤銷、正利
差表現及股票資本利得支撐台壽保 ROE 超過10%，現金股利殖利率4.5%

能源使用 
直接與間接能源消耗總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司運營範圍內消耗之能源總量 
- 能源使用總量 = 直接能源消耗總量 + 間接能源消耗量 
- 總能源使用量包括購買的能源、生產的能源 
- 就公用事業而言，輸電/電網損耗為其業務活動之一部分，被視為總能源消耗，數據不包括為滿足
能源使用而生產的電力（公用事業為出售而生產） 
- 就公用事業而言，用於能源生產的煤、天然氣或核能等原料不屬於「總能源使用」項下 
 
購買之再生能源 
Primary 再生能源購買總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司各種來源之能源消耗量與購買的能源中屬於自然界可再生者（太陽能、風能、水能、生物質
能、地熱能）之量  
- 如無證據顯示再生能源由公司生產，則所報告的能源數據視為購買的再生能源 
 
再生能源使用率 
再生能源占總能源消耗量之比例 
 
CO2 約當排放量 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸) 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合物 
(PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
公司員工人數與業務量於2015 年開
始大幅增加，使2015 年之後的溫室
氣體總排放量比過去明顯增加。未
來三年減碳目標訂定2021 年至
2023 年減少3.5%碳排總量。 
CO2 約當排放量營收比 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量（公噸）銷售（百萬元）比 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合物 
(PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
 
廢棄物總量 
廢棄物總量(公噸) 
- 總廢棄物 = 無害廢棄物 + 有害廢棄物 
- 僅考慮固體廢棄物，但如液體廢棄物以公噸為單位呈報，則會將其加入求得包含液體廢棄物之總
量 
- 對於採礦、石油與天然氣等行業，tailings、廢石、煤、飛灰等廢棄物亦考慮在內 
2020 年廢棄物處理支出金額約為新
臺幣420 萬元。未來中信金以2020
年為基準年，訂定2021 年至2023
年減少3.5%廢棄物總量。 
廢棄物回收率 
公司呈報的廢棄物回收率 
- 廢棄物回收率 = 廢棄物回收量/總廢棄物*100 
- 廢棄物轉化為能源或經由廢棄物焚燒產生能源視為廢棄物回收 
- 經由堆肥回收的廢棄物視為回收之廢棄物 
 
總取水量 
總取水量(立方公尺) 
- 由呈報組織直接或經水公司等中介機構從任何水源抽取的總水量 
- 水井、城鎮/公用事業/市政用水、河水、地表水等不同之水源均予以考慮 
營運用水無取用任何地下水，各辦
公大樓及營業據點用水僅供員工及
顧客使用，對水源未有負面影響。
未來三年節水目標訂定2021-2023
年用水總量減少3.5%。 
環保支出 
環保支出總金額 
- 所有用於環境保護，或防止、減少、控制環境因素、影響、危害的投資與支出，亦包括處置、處
理、衛生、清理支出 
 
員工流動率 
員工流動率 
- 包括任何原因（自願或非自願）離開公司的員工，如辭職、退休、自然離職/死亡、醫療失能、冗
員、裁員、重組、解僱、裁減或定期合約到期 
- 員工流動率 =（離開之員工/平均員工人數）*100 
- 平均員工人數 =（本年末員工人數 + 去年末員工人數）/2 
- 本財年末員工數 =上個財年末員工數 + 新員工數 - 離開之員工數 
 
女性經理 
女性經理百分比 
- 女性經理占公司經理的百分比 
- 如有不同階層之百分比，如最高階、高階、中階、初階，則會考慮中階女性經理之百分比 
- 女性經理百分比 = 女性經理人數/經理總數*100 
目前女性主管人數占所有主管人數
56.29%，其中中階主管及高階主管
的女性比例亦較2019 年成長了
2~3%。 
女性員工 
女性員工百分比 
- 女性員工占公司員工總數的百分比 
- 女性員工百分比 = 女性人數/員工總數*100 
 
教育訓練總時數 
所有員工教育訓練總時數 
- 僅考慮員工教育訓練時數 
- 包括一般員工所有類型的教育訓練（如健康與安全、環境、急難事件救援、技能與職業發展） 
- 如果數據以天為單位，則乘以 8，係假設 1 天 =  8 小時工作 
 
每位員工教育訓練時數

EC 晶片市佔率已各提升至45-50%及40-45%，持續分食美商市佔。

訪談內容 
1H23 EPS 4.84 元，年增11%優於預期，庫存領先同業落底 
聯陽1H23 營收30.32 億元，年增2%，毛利率55.4%，其中存貨跌價損失回沖約5,000 萬
元，一次性挹注毛利率1.65%，屏除此因素，常態毛利率53.7%，維持在長期50%以上的目
標，業外淨收益2,400 萬元，來自淨利息收入與匯兌收益，EPS 4.84 元，年增11%優於預期。 
存貨方面，聯陽2Q23 庫存僅8.2 億元，季減14%/年減39%，存貨週轉天數亦季減52 天至
104 天(同期180 天)，公司常態存貨週轉天數約90 多天，已回至健康可控水平，相較其他
NB/PC IC 設計公司，聯陽不論在庫存絕對金額或存貨週轉天數，均領先同業落底。 
產品組合方面，EC/IO 約50%、HSL 約30%、other 20%。

4Q23 步入淡季，估營收季減14% 
原估3Q23 營收季減0-5%，但聯陽受惠NB/PC 急單挹注，加上歐美返校需求優於預期，9 月
營收仍將些微月增，整體營收上修至2-3%，毛利率因存貨跌價損失回沖金額少於1H23，估
54%，EPS 2.73 元，展望4Q23，NB ODM 零組件拉貨高峰落在9-10 月，因此營收將開始
步入淡季，估15 億元，季減14%/年增31%，毛利率54.2%，EPS 1.97 元。 
2024 年NB 出貨量將年增5% 
雖然2023 年全球NB 出貨量連續第二年衰退至1.7 億台，年減13.7%，但我們預估2024 年
全球NB 出貨量有望重返成長軌道，年增5%至1.79 億台，說明如下： 
1. 換機週期：一般而言，NB 換機週期約為3~5 年，而在2020 年疫情爆發後NB 需求大增，
預期該批筆電可能自2024 年開始進入換機週期。 
2. 新興應用：包含Microsoft 365 Copilot 在內，新興AI 應用及技術進步導入決策與工作中，
商用型機種將在未來增添更多功能，為避免硬體成為運算頻頸，例如Intel 最新的筆電處理器
-Meteor Lake 亮點在於新增NPU(低功耗AI 引擎)，AI NB 並加強CPU、GPU，同時加大筆
電記憶體容量(一般NB 提高至DDR5-8GB 以上，商務與電競筆電則升級至DDR5-16G 以上)
規格大幅升級有助2024 年NB 換機潮。

2024 年NB/PC 回歸成長，Type-C PD 額外加分 
展望2024 年，我們看好NB/PC 產業重回成長，加上產業大者恆大，市占持續提升，帶動EC/IO
與高速影音介面相關晶片(HSL)出貨量提升，而Intel推出新世代CPU(Meteor Lake)，PC EC/IO
規格升級，亦有助整體混和ASP 持穩，新產品USB Type-C PD/HDMI 2.1 retimer 即將推出，
1H24 開始貢獻營收，估2024 年營收69 億元，年增10%，毛利率54.6%，EPS 11 元，年增
15%，細節說明如下： 
1. 
營收占比50%的PC EC/IO： 
甲、 為主晶片（CPU/PCH/SoC）IO 擴充套件，用於桌上型電腦輸出入控制晶片IC 稱
Super I/O，用於筆記型電腦內嵌式控制晶片IC 稱嵌入式控制器(Embedded 
controller, EC)，即可編程的 MCU，EC/IO 主要透過LPC 排線與CPU 溝通，主
要功能是做鍵盤控制/觸控板/電源管理/風扇控制/電池管理等功能，推估聯陽在
桌機Super I/O 晶片及NB 的EC 晶片在全球市佔率已各提升至45-50%及40-
45%，後續仍有提升空間，持續分食美商市佔。 
乙、 主要客戶涵蓋各大品牌如HP、聯想、ASUS、ACER，NB ODM 客戶則有廣達、
仁寶、英業達等。 
丙、 高單價高毛利率Type-C PD：過往主要供應商為美系德儀跟Cypress，德儀市佔
最高(佔多數)，目前聯陽也正式通過Intel 與AMD PD 認證，透過NB ODM 進到
供應鏈，USB Type-C PD 支援3.0/3.1 協定，也同時支援1 對1 與1 對2(1 顆
IC/2 個Port)，鎖定PC/NB 跟Docking 市場，產品主要在聯電8 吋廠投片，相
較於美商，性價比較高，消費型與商務NB 都有出，我們預估2024 年聯陽Type-
C PD 至少可拿10%以上市佔，初期貢獻營收3%。 
2. 
營收占比30%的高速影音介面相關晶片(HSL)：產品廣泛，包括Video Link、USB Video 
Bridge 等如HDMI、Display Port、 MIPI、High-Speed ADC/DAC 等，營運跟著PC/NB
連動外，亮點在HDMI 2.0 retimer 升級至HDMI 2.1 retimer，量價齊揚。 
3. 
營收占比5%的SoC：產品包括智慧家電/車載儀表/運動按摩/智能樓宇，用於上述產品
的彩色顯示控制板，聯陽產品優勢在於開機速度較同業快(僅1-2 秒)，且人機介面豐富，
裝置穩定性亦高，我們預估營運穩健向上。

公司簡介 
公司成立於1996 年，為全球輸出入(I/O)控制IC 領導廠商，由聯電RD 部門分割出來，是聯
電旗下轉投資，2008 合併聯盛半導體、繪展科技、晶瀚科技。截至2023 年，大股東聯電持
股維持8.7%不變，聯陽主要產品為桌上型電腦輸出入控制晶片系列IC(Super IO)、筆記型電
腦內嵌式控制晶片系列 IC(Embedded controller)、高速影音介面相關晶片系列IC、系統單
晶片SoC、其他客製化應用晶片，產品組合為EC/IO 50%(主要應用於DT/NB、橋接相關IC)、
高速影音介面HSL 30%(HDMI/Display Port/USB-C/MIPI 控制IC)、Others 20%(數位電視
接收、ccHDTV 傳輸及接收相關IC、可視門鈴及智慧控制板相關IC 等)。

一、營運與財務概況 
1. 
3Q25 毛利率67%。但在疫情紅利過後，營運還是持續有阻
力，目前是虧損狀態。而虧損原因也有為了第二成長動能所
進行的戰略性研發投入。 
2. 
區域別營收：以外銷為主，過往(2018)東南亞32%、中國30%
為兩大主要市場。而近年為避免與低價產品競爭，營運重心
已從中國策略性轉移至東南亞，3Q25 東南亞市場佔比已提
升至54%。 
二、產品與業務結構 
1. 
核心優勢：獨創iiPCR 技術、提供萃取→擴增→判讀的一站
式方案，並具備跨領域整合能力(分子生物/光機電/軟體/精
密製造)，及擁有國際認證。 
2. 
產品組合：水產養殖(佔營收45%)、畜產(30%多)、伴侶動
物(10%多)、IVD 人用和其他。 
3. 
水產養殖為核心業務預期穩定成長，畜產是重點發展業務
(主要東南亞市場)，伴侶動物是新興成長動能。 
4. 
第一曲線深化(2025-2026 短期策略)：聚焦東南亞，鎖定豬
隻、禽類、水產養殖三大產業，提供整合性解決方案。 
5. 
核心機台：POCKIT Central 自動化核酸分析儀，及手持式
POCKIT Micro 系列。 
三、第二成長曲線啟動(NGS 建庫市場與SATLite) 
1. 
過去10 年，定序成本快速下降，但建庫成本變化不大。建
庫成為定序流程中的瓶頸。 
2. 
市場困境：手動建庫耗時費力，需4~8 小時高度集中操作，
且易於出錯、重複性差。而現有自動化，主流設備設計用於
8~96 樣本，導致少量樣本必須湊批才能符合成本效益，犧
牲了時效性。 
3. 
解決方案：SATLite 自動化建庫系統 
定位：鎖定「低通量、即時反應」需求，是為所有實驗室提
供即時結果的快速反應平台。專為1~4 個樣本設計，重量約 
25 公斤左右。

Background: We met with Taiwan Surface Mounting Technology (TSMT)’s 
management on 21 May (see our 13 May flash). Per management, its 
product mix for 2025 was: TFT-LCD 46%, Mini LED 11%, DRAM module 
16%, auto 9%, cable 9%, touch 5%, and others 4%. Management guides 
for the mix for 2026 to be: TFT-LCD 46%, Mini LED 11%, DRAM module 
17%, auto 8%, cable 6%, touch 5%, and others 7%. The QFII holding of 
TSMT was 18.2% on 20 May vs 19.8% at the end of 2025. 
 
Highlights: 2026-27 guidance. TSMT guides for YoY revenue growth of 5-
10% (close to the high end; +1.9% YoY revenue growth for 4M26) for 2026 
and a double-digit % YoY growth for 2027, thanks to the multiple revenue 
drivers from AI-related demand. For 2026, the company expects gross 
margin of 13-15% (up QoQ; vs 12.8% gross margin in 2025), with further 
YoY growth in 2027 on a more favourable product mix. Its AI-related 
revenue target is 15-20% for 2027, up from 5-6% in 4Q26 and 1-2% in 
2026. For 2026, the company expects 2H26 revenue to be higher than that 
in 1H26, thanks to the rising order outlook from DRAM modules and AI-
related revenue supported by its capacity ramping up from its Mexico, 
India, and Vietnam plants. 
 
Multiple revenue drivers to kick off from 2H26. TSMT mentioned several 
revenue drivers as follows: 1) Optical transceiver assembly. TSMT will be 
the major supplier of 800G and 1.6T products to its US-based client, and 
the company has seen some outsourcing demand from China-based 
clients, with 4-5% of combined revenue contribution in 4Q26. 2) DRAM 
module. TSMT expects the revenue contribution to rise to 20-25% in 2H26, 
up from 18% in 2Q26, and to grow YoY in 2027 considering its US- and 
China-based clients. 3) Low earth orbit (LEO). TSMT will start delivering 
SMT products in 2H26 for a US-based client. 4) Humanoid robots. The 
company sees business opportunity (sensor modules and PCBA) from the 
US-based client with revenue contribution from 2027, likely to reach a low 
single-digit % of 2027 revenue. 5) Battery backup unit (BBU). The 
company will trial run products in 4Q26 or 2027. 6) Server SMT. Currently, 
TSMT has two clients and plans to add a new one in 2H26 from Taiwan or 
the US. Thus, the company guides for capex of USD100-150m over 2026-
27, up from USD100m in 2025, subject to its capacity expansion plan in 
Mexico, as it expects capacity constraints for SMT in the next 1-2 years 
due to the increasing use of AI applications. The company also plans to 
expand its production capacity in China, Vietnam, Taiwan, and Mexico. 
 
Valuation: The stock is currently trading at PERs of 21.4x and 17.4x based 
on the Bloomberg consensus’ 2026E and 2027E EPS, respectively.

GS Factor Profile 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) 
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, 
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

成長。自1 月起併表的新富生光電 (中) 營收貢獻預計自 2Q26 起加速成
長，管理層表示其光通訊產品已進入初期放量階段。此外，公司車用與工業
應用需求亦逐步回溫，尤其是工廠自動化與機器人領域。 
2027 年 EPS 預估維持不變。我們新增2028 年 EPS 預估為145.75 元，隱
含2025-28 年 EPS CAGR 達 46%；同時下修 2026 年 EPS 預估10%，反映
短期毛利率逆風。我們仍看好貿聯在 HPC 領域橫跨電源、銅纜與光纖的完
整產品布局，預估 2025-28 年HPC 營收 CAGR 為76%，其中電源線與資
料線分別成長79%、73%。

凱基重申貿聯「增加持股」評等與12 個月目標價2,600 元，基於2027 年
完全稀釋EPS 預估的25 倍 (目標本益比不變)。我們認為短期不利因素提供
進場良機，建議股價逢回布局。

能源使用 
直接與間接能源消耗總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司運營範圍內消耗之能源總量 
- 能源使用總量 = 直接能源消耗總量 + 間接能源消耗量 
- 總能源使用量包括購買的能源、生產的能源 
- 就公用事業而言，輸電/電網損耗為其業務活動之一部分，被視為總能源消耗，數據不包括
為滿足能源使用而生產的電力（公用事業為出售而生產） 
- 就公用事業而言，用於能源生產的煤、天然氣或核能等原料不屬於「總能源使用」項下 
 
購買之再生能源 
Primary 再生能源購買總量(十億焦耳) 
- 公司各種來源之能源消耗量與購買的能源中屬於自然界可再生者（太陽能、風能、水能、
生物質能、地熱能）之量  
- 如無證據顯示再生能源由公司生產，則所報告的能源數據視為購買的再生能源 
 
再生能源使用率 
再生能源占總能源消耗量之比例 
 
CO2 約當排放量 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量(公噸) 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合
物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
 
CO2 約當排放量營收比 
直接 CO2 與 CO2 約當排放量（公噸）銷售（百萬元）比 
- 公司擁有或控制的來源的直接排放量（範圍 1 排放量） 
- 相關氣體：二氧化碳 (CO2)、甲烷 (CH4)、一氧化二氮 (N2O)、氫氟碳化物 (HFCS)、全氟化合
物 (PFCS)、六氟化硫 (SF6)、三氟化氮 (NF3) 
 
廢棄物總量 
廢棄物總量(公噸) 
- 總廢棄物 = 無害廢棄物 + 有害廢棄物 
- 僅考慮固體廢棄物，但如液體廢棄物以公噸為單位呈報，則會將其加入求得包含液體廢棄
物之總量 
- 對於採礦、石油與天然氣等行業，tailings、廢石、煤、飛灰等廢棄物亦考慮在內 
 
廢棄物回收率 
公司呈報的廢棄物回收率 
- 廢棄物回收率 = 廢棄物回收量/總廢棄物*100 
- 廢棄物轉化為能源或經由廢棄物焚燒產生能源視為廢棄物回收 
- 經由堆肥回收的廢棄物視為回收之廢棄物 
 
總取水量 
總取水量(立方公尺) 
- 由呈報組織直接或經水公司等中介機構從任何水源抽取的總水量 
- 水井、城鎮/公用事業/市政用水、河水、地表水等不同之水源均予以考慮 
 
環保支出 
環保支出總金額 
- 所有用於環境保護，或防止、減少、控制環境因素、影響、危害的投資與支出，亦包括處
置、處理、衛生、清理支出 
 
員工流動率 
員工流動率 
- 包括任何原因（自願或非自願）離開公司的員工，如辭職、退休、自然離職/死亡、醫療失
能、冗員、裁員、重組、解僱、裁減或定期合約到期 
- 員工流動率 =（離開之員工/平均員工人數）*100 
- 平均員工人數 =（本年末員工人數 + 去年末員工人數）/2 
- 本財年末員工數 =上個財年末員工數 + 新員工數 - 離開之員工數 
 
女性經理 
女性經理百分比 
- 女性經理占公司經理的百分比 
- 如有不同階層之百分比，如最高階、高階、中階、初階，則會考慮中階女性經理之百分比 
- 女性經理百分比 = 女性經理人數/經理總數*100 
 
女性員工 
女性員工百分比 
- 女性員工占公司員工總數的百分比 
- 女性員工百分比 = 女性人數/員工總數*100 
 
教育訓練總時數 
所有員工教育訓練總時數 
- 僅考慮員工教育訓練時數 
- 包括一般員工所有類型的教育訓練（如健康與安全、環境、急難事件救援、技能與職業發
展） 
- 如果數據以天為單位，則乘以 8，係假設 1 天 =  8 小時工作

Smoother transition
Expect better-than-feared 4Q25 and promising 2026 outlook
We forecast Wiwynn’s September sales to be NT$85.0bn (-11% MoM, +146% YoY) 
thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs. While the 
market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from 
4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up
for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this. We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico 
facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will 
further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26. We lift 
25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200. Maintain 
Outperform.
3Q25 preview
Driven by increased cloud Capex, Wiwynn as the major AWS ASIC L10/L11 supplier
has continued to benefit from ASIC demand. With ongoing robust shipments for 
AWS Trainium2, we forecast September sales of NT$85.0bn, -11% MoM, +146% 
YoY, thanks to the robust demand for AWS ASICs, and this will lead to 3Q25CT
revenue of NT$266bn, which is 17% higher than consensus forecasts.
AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated
While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition 
from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to 
mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers. We see continued
strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25. And for Oracle’s orders, 
Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11. We expect 
the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026
with upside risk.
Stronger 2026 outlook
As new US capacity comes online in end-4Q25/early-1Q26, Wiwynn will complete 
the manufacturing support for key customers’ AI server demand under the current 
uncertain US tariff conditions. Its US plant will focus on production of liquid cooling 
server racks, in line with the trend of ASIC liquid cooling adoption from 4Q25 
onwards. Into 2026, with AWS’ rising ASIC demand for Trainium3 and ongoing order
share wins in GPU racks, we forecast 2026 sales to grow 10% YoY.
Earnings revisions and valuation
We lift 25/26/27CT EPS by 6%/14%/18% to reflect the strong near-term demand 
from AWS Trainium2, higher revenue contribution from AWS Trainium3 and 
Oracle’s GPU server shipments, resulting in a higher TP of NT$4,200 (from 
NT$3,600), still based on 16x 26CT PE. Maintain Outperform.

Investment thesis
Expect it to benefit from strong CSP ASIC server demand in 2025; new server 
platform ramp-ups and accelerating ASIC server shipments. Risk-reward looks 
favourable even if there is no AI contribution from the Middle East.
Catalysts
1) Stronger-than-expected ASIC server demand; 2) faster-than-expected general 
server shipment ramp-up; 3) better-than-expected Middle East contribution.
Valuation details
Our target price is based on a PE valuation methodology as we believe it better 
reflects market expectations for the company’s earnings growth outlook. Our target 
price is based on 16x 2026CT PE, 1sd above the five-year average PE, to factor in 
stronger AI and ASIC server demand despite the removal of the Middle East 
contribution. We believe a 16x PE is justified given its 51% EPS Cagr over 24-27CT.
Investment risks
Risks include 1) a slowdown in CSP clients’ Capex investment, which could lead to 
a more subdued revenue outlook; 2) intensifying competition in datacentre 
hardware that may result in order loss and/or margin pressure; 3) slower-than-
expected ramp-up of new business development, especially in new client and AI 
penetration, that could lead to a more volatile earnings profile; and 4) short supply 
of key components that would impede the schedule for product shipments and the 
revenue outlook.

內容摘要 
 
受惠彩色電子紙電子書閱讀器需求強勁，今年前三季EPS 3.72元  
今年第三季營收22.96億元，季增約11%、年增約26%，為2024年第
一季以來單季新高，主要來自匯率回穩與產品組合優化。受惠彩色電
子紙電子書閱讀器需求強勁，帶動營運連續走升，惟2025上半年業外
損失較嚴重，累計今年前三季EPS 3.72元。  
 
 第四季為閱讀器傳統旺季，預期明年營收可望再雙位數成長  
展望後市，振曜看好今年第四季為閱讀器傳統旺季，加上10月營收已
創今年單月新高、6月以來逐月走揚，2025全年營收可望改寫歷史紀
錄。隨彩色閱讀器比重上升、看板業務放大以及轉投資效益持續發

GS Factor Proﬁle 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Proﬁle provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our coverage universe) and its 
sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial 
Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for speciﬁc metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the ﬁscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for ﬁnancial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for ﬁnancial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher ﬁnancial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for ﬁnancial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the ﬁscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the ﬁscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Proﬁle, please contact your GS representative.  
M&A Rank 
Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary 
across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring 
companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 
representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard 
departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not 
factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

coming years, we expect its AI servers revenues contribution to reach up to 16% / 
28% / 35% in 2026-28E, riding on the diversifying AI servers trend, and the 
company’s capacity expansion across US, Taiwan, and Vietnam. The company’s 
capacity expansion in Taiwan started in Oct, supporting the Oct revenues MoM 
increase (+21% MoM), followed by Vietnam capacity expansion in 1Q26, and US 
capacity expansion in mid 2026. During SC25 (Super Computing Conference 2025, 
link) in Nov, Mitac showcased their AI servers across training and inferencing, across 
liquid cooled and air cooled, and across NVIDIA and AMD platforms. We expect 
Mitac’s strong design capability and close work with its major US CSP customer, 
could support its business expansion, from networking racks to AI servers, driving its 
OP income to grow at 33% CAGR in 2025-28E post the turn around in 2024A, 
supporting the valuation re-rating. Maintain Buy.

GS Factor Profile 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) 
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, 
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns

Background: We had an update with the management team on 30 
September. Founded in 1987 and listed on Taiwan’s main board in 2009, 
Jentech is a manufacturer of cooling products (74% of 1H25 revenue vs. 
66% in 2024, including heat spreader for server/AI server), lead frames 
(9% of 1H25 revenue vs. 14% in 2024), electronic components (6% of 
1H25 revenue vs. 9% in 2024), communication connectors (1% of 1H25 
revenue vs. 2% in 2024) and others (10% of 1H25 revenue vs. 10% in 
2024). The company has production sites in Taiwan and China, with a new 
plant currently under construction in Taoyuan Aerotropolis (Taiwan) mainly 
for the production of heat spreaders, cooling baseplates and server loading 
mechanisms. Jentech’s QFII holdings percentage was 28.4% as of 2 
October 2025, vs. 25.7% at the beginning of 2025. 
 
Highlights: Jentech's next-generation thermal product offerings 
include the Vapor Chamber Lid (VCL) and the Microchannel Lid (MCL). 
MCL is a chip-level cooling solution, which enables the heat removal 
required to meet the enormous thermal loads of today’s AI servers. There is 
still discussion on whether the next-generation AI platform will adopt MCL 
technology, while holding a possibility that the initial rollout may begin with 
VCL, followed by a subsequent MCL version. However, there is no final 
decision yet. 
 
Competitive edge. Jentech has a vertical integration model for its cooling 
products which incorporates elements such as design capability, mould 
processing, semiconductor level plating, machining, stamping, and injection 
moulding. Its MCL offering is designed for chip-level thermal management 
and is its highly differentiated vs. other products on the market, which sets 
a high entry barrier for its competitors. Jentech’s competitive edges: 1) Its 
equipment and process architecture are purpose-built for heat spreader 
manufacturing, reflecting a bespoke, application-driven production 
approach; 2) the firm demonstrates deep mastery of material, which 
underpins consistent product performance; 3) the operational focus on yield 
improvement directly translates into margin expansion, making process 
control a lever for profitability. Notably, the company achieves 
semiconductor-grade cleanliness not through a traditional cleanroom but 
via specialised cleaning technologies, allowing it to meet stringent quality 
requirements for its chip-level products. Jentech reported revenue of 
TWD13.3bn (+53.8% YoY) for 8M25, mainly driven by its cooling products 
for AI servers. 
 
Valuation: Per Bloomberg consensus, the stock is trading at 2025/26E 
PERs of 64.1x/41.3x, vs. its past-3-year forward trading range of 17-47x.

What’s new: Tong Yang released its 9M23 operating data on 11 October, 
having released its 9M23 revenue data on 4 October (see our memo). We 
believe the increasing adoption of after-market (AM) components in the US 
is likely to make it a structural trend, which we see as a mid-to-long-term 
revenue driver. However, in the near term, we believe the upward EPS 
revision trend will be the share-price catalyst. We reaffirm our Buy (1) call. 
What’s the impact: Record-high quarterly EPS in 3Q23, mainly thanks 
to revenue, gross margin and operating margin beat. Tong Yang’s 
3Q23 revenue of TWD6,154m (+10.9% QoQ and +11.3% YoY) was ahead 
of our forecast and the consensus estimate by 6.1% and 4.8%, 
respectively, mainly due to the solid AM revenue and recovery in China 
OEM revenue. Its operating margin came in at 16.5% in 3Q23, ahead of 
our (14.9%) and the consensus (14.7%) forecasts. Its operating profit of 
TWD1,018m (+27.8% QoQ and +82.4% YoY) beat both our and the 
consensus forecasts by 17.6%, which we attribute to the upbeat gross 
margin from the AM business with improving operating leverage. With an 
FX gain of TWD187.4m, Tong Yang’s pre-tax profit of TWD1,238m (+30.4% 
QoQ and +43.4% YoY) beat our and the consensus estimates by 16.9% 
and 23.3%, respectively. Its gross margin was c.30% in 3Q23 (vs. our 
forecast of 28.9% and the consensus forecast of 28.8%), up from 29.0% in 
2Q23 and 24.6% in 3Q22. 
Solid order outlook for AM segment plus recovery of China OEM 
segment. Tong Yang’s AM order demand remains solid, especially from the 
US, Europe and Central and South America, thanks to the upcoming peak 
season and the promotion from State Farm AM adoption, which should be 
the key earnings driver for Tong Yang. Its OEM revenue improved MoM in 
September 2023 and we expect the momentum to carry forward into 4Q23, 
with an improving gross margin. We revise up our 2023-25E EPS by 6-7%, 
mainly after factoring in our more aggressive revenue and margin 
assumptions. 
What we recommend: We reaffirm our Buy (1) call and raise our 12-month 
TP to TWD100 (from TWD91), still based on a target PER of 18x applied to 
our 1-year forward EPS, backed by an accelerating earnings momentum 
over 2023-25E and a likely structural trend that will lift the AM penetration 
rate in the US. Our target PER is around the average of the stock’s past-3-
year range of 7-31x. Key downside risks: weaker-than-expected gross-
margin expansion and AM revenue. 
How we differ: Our 2023-25E EPS are 4-10% above the consensus, likely 
as we are more aggressive on its revenue and gross margin expansion.

GMs, despite unprecedentedly steep TWD appreciation and increased overseas Fab 
dilution. We expect 4Q25 to be the GM trough (due to UTR draw-down), with GMs 
likely to rebound in 2026 with price hikes, better N3 yield and accelerated productivity 
and cost-down measures. Demand trends for AI are strong with broader demand 
pickup (CSPs, sovereign AI and China demand) and CoWoS capacity likely to remain 
tight into 2026. While TSMC is cautious on 4Q25 (we now model 6% qoq decline in 
revenues), chances are that demand could shape up better if tariffs turn out to be less 
intense than feared. As such, we believe TSMC could eventually finish the year with 
low-mid 30% yoy growth in USD terms (JPMe 32%). We continue to see healthy 
growth in 2026, with a faster N2 ramp, price hikes from1Q26 and continued strength 
in N3 due to strong AI accelerator demand. We raise our FY25/ FY26 EPS estimates 
by 5/4% to reflect stronger growth prospects in AI and stay OW with a Dec-25 PT of 
NT$1,275. In the near term, we believe the stock may stay rangebound as the market 
is likely to focus on Sec 232 and specific country tariff outcomes. Once some clarity 
emerges on this front, we believe the stock should start pricing in strong growth and 
GM rebound in 2026, with some prospect of meaningful N2 outsourcing from Intel.

Summary Investment Thesis and Valuation
Investment Thesis
We expect TSMC's structural growth drivers to remain strong 
due to its near-monopoly position in AI accelerators and edge 
AI, supported by its robust process roadmap (N3 and N2) and 
industry-leading packaging technology. We believe TSMC 
could grow low-mid 30% in USD terms in 2025 and healthy 
growth in 2026, driven by broader AI demand pick-up (e.g. 
CSPs, sovereigns and China demand) with CoWoS capacity 
remaining tight into 2026. Additionally, we anticipate the GM to 
rebound in 2026 with price hikes, better N3 yield, and 
accelerated productivity and cost-down measures.
Valuation
Our Dec-25 PT of NT$1,275 is based on ~20x 12-month forward 
P/E and reflects the positive fundamental demand driver, 
continued growth in N3 and stronger N2 ramp in 2026. Our 
target multiple is higher than TSMC’s five-year average 
historical multiple.

Passing the GM test; 2026 should look better
TSMC reported a stronger-than-expected 2Q GM of 58.6%, beating both JPMe and 
Consensus by 0.7-1ppt and reaching the high-end of its guidance (57-59%) despite 
unfavorable FX (around 125bps impact) thanks to higher-than-expected UTR and cost 
improvement efforts.  
Company guided 3Q rev to grow 8% qoq at mid point, with GM likely at 55.5-57.5% 
(down 2.1ppts qoq at mid point). The margin guidance is quite impressive in our view, 
considering a 600 bps drag from TWD and 100-200bps from overseas expansion since 
1Q25. 
While 4Q GM would likely further decline with the UTR draw down, we expect 4Q25 
to be the near-term bottom for GMs. 
2H25 should be the period with maximum stress on GMs (fastest period of TWD 
appreciation so far in 3Q25, overseas cost dilution, some negate demand impact 
dragging utilization lower in 4Q25 with price hikes not kicking in yet).  Even in this 
period, TSMC appears to be able to hold GMs well above 53%, demonstrating its 
underlying pricing power and operational efficiency. Without the recent TWD 
appreciation, we believe TSMC would have been able to achieve 60+% GMs at this 
point. 
With price hikes and a better N3 mix kicking in from early 2026, we expect GMs to 
remain higher than 2H25 levels through 2026, despite some dilution in late 2026 as N2 
starts ramping up.

Pricing uptick coming through; Double-digit blended ASP 
increases now the norm
TSMC has now seen more than 10 quarters of double-digit YoY ASP increases, 
including a 16% YoY rise in 2Q25. Given strong pricing power and intention to raise 
pricing to reflect increasing costs and technology leadership, we believe that low-mid 
teens blended ASP growth will become the norm for TSMC moving forward. As a 
result, a 5-6% increase in wafer shipments should contribute to ~20% revenue growth, 
which in turn should likely reduce capital intensity and support strong 30+% ROE over 
the long term.
With TSMC indicating that capacity remains tight, particularly for N5 and N3, and a 
faster ramp-up of N2, we anticipate pricing to rise in 2026 (6-10% increase in leading-
edge wafer prices, along with higher pricing for overseas fabs) to offset cost increases, 
some impact of TWD appreciation and overseas expansion.

Near-term eyes largely on tariffs and the degree of weakness 
in 4Q
In the earnings call, TSMC raised 2025 full year guidance to 30% yoy revenue growth 
in USD terms, from previous guidance of mid- 20s. While we’ve already highlighted the 
potential guidance raise (link), the magnitude turns out to be slightly above our 
expectation of high-20s.
Investor attention is likely to be largely focused on the implied qoq weakness (around 
10% qoq revenue decline) in 4Q, which is weaker than Consensus and previous JPMe of 
1%/6% qoq decline. We believe the implied weakness is mainly due to 1) high base in 
3Q (rev guidance above market expectations), 2) TSMC taking a conservative view on 
tariffs (Sec 232 and country-specific tariffs) and not factoring in any exemptions for 
TSMC or Taiwan-made products at this point, and 3) TSMC also appears to be 
anticipating a marked slowdown in consumer demand as a result (including iPhone, in 
our view).
However, we feel that such a sharp slowdown in demand may not materialize, given that 
tariff outcomes so far have been better than feared. While we do believe that there has 
been some pull-in demand, especially in consumer electronics, in 1H25 (1H rev up 40% 
yoy in USD terms), but the extent is likely small given the ongoing tightness in N5 and 
N3 capacity since 2H24.
We therefore maintain our 6% qoq decline expectation for 4Q, and expect TSMC to 
eventually finish the year with low-mid 30% yoy growth in USD terms (JPMe 32%).

Capex outlook and Dividend growth 
TSMC maintained its 2025 Capex guidance unchanged at US$38-42bn (up ~30% yoy). 
While there’s no further guidance for coming years yet, management only indicated no 
significant drop in Capex expected, despite very strong N2 demand, which is a bit more 
guarded, compared to investors’ expectation of capex increase in 2026.
However, we still anticipate continued Capex growth to US$45bn (up 13% yoy) 
in 2026, and maintained at a high level in 2027 (JPMe~US$40bn) driven by 1) strong 
N2 demand, 2) continued strength in N3, and 3) continued accelerated buildout of 
capacity in the US (tools move in for the 2nd AZ Fab and construction of 3rd and 
4th AZ Fab in 2026). In addition, we expect N2 demand to be upsized in case Intel signs 
a capacity agreement with TSMC for large-scale N2 outsourcing. 
While the Capex seems to be high in terms of dollar amount, management also 
emphasized that sales growth would outgrow the capex growth. We anticipate capital 
intensity likely to be down to ~30% in 2027 versus 40-50% in 2023-25. 
Meanwhile, we believe that TSMC’s cash dividends should grow steadily due to strong 
FCF generation, and expect a 2023-27 DPS CAGR of 26%, with 2027E dividends 
reaching NT$33 levels.

Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks
TSMC (Overweight; Price Target: NT$1275.0)
Investment Thesis
We expect TSMC's structural growth drivers to remain strong due to its near-monopoly 
position in AI accelerators and edge AI, supported by its robust process roadmap (N3 and 
N2) and industry-leading packaging technology. We believe TSMC could grow low-mid 
30% in USD terms in 2025 and healthy growth in 2026, driven by broader AI demand pick-
up (e.g. CSPs, sovereigns and China demand) with CoWoS capacity remaining tight into 
2026. Additionally, we anticipate the GM to rebound in 2026 with price hikes, better N3 
yield, and accelerated productivity and cost-down measures.
Valuation
Our Dec-25 PT of NT$1,275 is based on ~20x 12-month forward P/E and reflects the 
positive fundamental demand driver, continued growth in N3 and stronger N2 ramp in 2026. 
Our target multiple is higher than TSMC’s five-year average historical multiple.
Risks to Rating and Price Target
Key downside risks to our rating and price target include: (1) uncertainty regarding the 
impact of tariffs and a global economic slowdown; (2) worse-than-expected AI demand in 
2026; and (3) greater GM dilution from US fabs due to the faster ramp.

Dual growth engines moving into focus  
We are turning more constructive on Silergy and upgrading the stock 
to Buy from Neutral, as we believe the company is entering a new 
earnings upcycle driven by 1) stronger-than-expected data 
centers demand, which we expect to contribute 15-20% of revenue 
in 2026E (vs. less than 10% in 2025), with further upside into 
2027/2028, 2) continued growth in automotive content, with 
Silergy’s dollar content per vehicle expected to more than double in 
2026, which in our view should drive auto revenue growth of more 
than 50% YoY this year, and 3) higher structural GM, supported by 
more favorable product mix and rising penetration of Gen 4 
products, underpinned by strength in auto and data center 
applications. Overall, we revise up our 2026/2027E earnings by 
35-61% and expect 72% earnings CAGR in 2025-2028E.
Growth is now back on track 
We believe analog is entering a new upcycle, with demand 
expanding beyond a purely cyclical rebound. Silergy’s growth profile 
is shifting from a consumer-driven recovery toward a structural 
story underpinned by auto and data center demand. Management 
is now confident of achieving at least 20% YoY revenue growth in 
2026, returning to its long-term 20-30% growth target after a 
subdued 2025 (revenue up only 1.9% YoY). Management also 
highlighted data center and automotive segments as the company’s 
main growth drivers, with new product dollar content ramping faster 
than expected, supported by higher chip power consumption and 
strong EV/hybrid EV demand. 
Net net, we now forecast Silergy’s 2026-2028E revenue to grow 
25%/32%/28% YoY, with GM improving to 51.0%/54.8%/55.5%. 
Following our earnings revisions, we raise our 12m TP to NT$650 
from NT$310 (30x 2027E EPS), which implies c.39% upside — we 
upgrade to Buy from Neutral.

1Q26 GM miss on inventory impairment 
Silergy hosted its 1Q26 analyst meeting on May 15. 1Q26 revenue was NT$4,860mn 
(-9.9% QoQ, +18.7% YoY), which came in slightly above GSe and inline with Bloomberg 
consensus. In terms of margins, 1Q26 GM of 48.2% (down 2.97ppts QoQ) missed 
GSe/Bloomberg consensus of 51.9%/51.5%, mainly due to 1) inventory impairment loss, 
which impacted GM by 1.6ppts, 2) product mix, with higher revenue contribution from 
PCs and less from auto-related applications, and 3) higher upstream cost with some 
price hikes seen in 1Q26 from foundry. Looking ahead, management expects the current 
inventory impairment loss to reverse in future periods as the underlying products are 
sold through. Overall, Silergy 1Q26 core ops came in largely inline with GSe yet missed 
Bloomberg consensus by 28%. However, Silergy’s 1Q26 EPS of NT$1.98 still came in 
higher vs. GSe/Bloomberg consensus due to higher non-op gain. 
Data center power IC entering a rapid growth phase 
We view data centers as Silergy’s most important incremental growth driver. 
Management indicated that data center revenue grew 90% YoY in 1Q26 and reached 
15% of total revenue, up from a single-digit contribution in 2025. The main drivers are 
PMICs used on server motherboards, as well as peripheral applications such as optical 
modules. For PMICs, management expects dollar content to scale linearly with GPU 
power consumption, which is more than doubling every three years. In our view, the 
current ramp in server PMIC solutions is primarily tied to general-purpose server 
applications for mainland China customers, while AI-related programs are still in the 
qualification stage and should see more meaningful volume ramp-up from 2027. In 
optical modules, management now expects content value to rise as the market 
transitions from 400G to 800G and 1.6T. As power density and board complexity 
continue to increase, we believe this should support higher power management content 
per system. Overall, we expect Silergy’s server-related revenue exposure to increase 
rapidly to 15-20% in 2026E, from less than 10% in 2025, with further upside into 2027E 
and 2028E. 
Auto dollar content expansion supports a second structural leg 
Beyond data centers, we view automotive as another key structural growth driver for 
Silergy. Management noted that automotive revenue grew 20% YoY in 1Q26, supported 
primarily by robust demand from China EV and hybrid platforms, new product launches, 
and customer share gains. The company expects automotive to account for 15-20% of 
revenue in 2026, up from 13.6% in 2025. More importantly, Silergy’s addressable dollar 
content per vehicle continues to expand. Management indicated that dollar content had 
reached around $120 per car by end-2025 and could rise to approximately $250 by 
end-2026, driven by higher EV and hybrid penetration as well as increasing power 
management content per vehicle. In our view, this underpins a more durable growth 
trajectory than a simple cyclical analog recovery, as Silergy is positioned to benefit not 
only from vehicle production growth but also from rising content per car. Overall, we 
expect Silergy’s automotive business to deliver a 61% CAGR over 2025-2028E, with 
revenue mix reaching the high-20% range by 2028E. 
Margin profile improving as Gen 4 penetration increase 
We expect Silergy’s GM profile to improve over 2026-2028E despite the weakness seen 
in 1Q26, driven primarily by a richer mix of higher-margin Gen 4 products. Management

Key risks to our views 
1) Slower demand recovery: A change in pace of demand recovery would likely result

Investment Thesis - Silergy (6415.TW) 
Silergy is a leading domestic PMIC design house, and we remain constructive on its 
long-term growth outlook as the company continues to expand into higher-end 
applications such as servers/datacenter, HPC, and automotive. We expect Silergy to 
return to its long-term revenue growth trajectory of 20-30% YoY over the coming years, 
supported by continued dollar-content expansion in both the datacenter and 
automotive segments. As revenue contribution from these businesses increases, we 
believe Silergy’s gross margin profile should improve structurally, driven by the rising 
penetration of margin-accretive Gen 4 solutions. Overall, Silergy is currently trading 
below its historical upcycle valuation of 30x FY27E P/E, which we view as an attractive 
entry point. We therefore maintain a Buy rating on the stock. 
Price Target Risks and Methodology  
Valuation: Our 12m TP is NT$650, based on a target P/E of 30x (inline with its historical 
upcycle P/E) applied to our 2027E EPS. 
Key risks to our views: 1) Slower end-demand recovery, 2) Worse-than-expected cost 
controls, 3) slower progress with new addressable markets, 4) an intensifying 
competition landscape, and 5) geopolitical risks.

GS Factor Profile 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) 
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, 
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.  
M&A Rank 
Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary 
across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring 
companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 
representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard 
departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not 
factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

GS Factor Profile 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) 
and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, 
Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.  
M&A Rank 
Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary 
across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring 
companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 
representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard 
departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not 
factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

through price hikes from April (lagging peers) with broad

recovery.

EMC, a key supplier of high-end HDI material (70%+ market share) and SLP material 
(90%+ market share), has been focusing on the high-speed switch/server CCL market for 
3-5+ years. We are positive on its market share trajectory in the server industry and
expect EMC to increase its share from <10% in the Purley generation to 15-20%/20+%
in the Whitley/Eagle Stream platforms. EMC is also proactively expanding its share in the
switch market (40%/30%+ in 2024/23 vs. <5% before 2019), with an expanding AI
customer base (only one 400G customer in 3Q20, to being one of the largest suppliers in
2023), which should continue to benefit the company’s top/bottom line growth over
time. We believe EMC’s leading position in the AI server CCL market should drive strong
revenue growth and GM/OPM expansion in the long term, given that it is the major
supplier for all Nvidia/Google/AWS AI server projects, and we expect it to maintain its
leadership position. Considering its leading position in the high-end CCL industry, solid
production skills and earnings growth outlook, we are Buy rated on the stock. With the
shares trading at a 2026E P/E below AI server component suppliers and supported by a
solid growth outlook, we view valuation as attractive.

rising trade tensions, which could lead to weaker smartphone and server shipments; and 
(3) rising competition from mainland China peers.

In this note, we address the key FAQs from investors on Jentech after we initiated 
coverage on September 29 (link).
•
What is already priced into Jentech’s current share price? What is not yet 
factored-in which could drive further outperformance in its share price? 
Despite Jentech’s share price being up ~60% YTD vs Taiex’s 15%, we don’t 
sense that the market has priced in the opportunities of micro-channel lid to AI 
chips adoption soon. This is based on the majority feedback from our buy side 
customers, and their consensus is that micro-channel lid will be adopted in 
2H27 at the earliest. Second, micro-channel lid is a product that can replace the 
current cold plate module, but AVC (3017.TW), the biggest cold plate module 
maker’s share price is up ~80% YTD. We are more constructive vs. the Street 
on the adoption of micro-channel lid to start from 2H26 and become more 
mainstream in 2027 (details in below paragraphs), while Jentech will be the 
sole supplier in the first year of adoption and can still maintain its leadership 
in the upcoming years, given its solid technology leadership in the packaging-
level cooling solutions, especially for AI server chips. We believe any further 
confirmation in the upcoming months will be a major share price driver. On the 
other hand, we believe Jentech is one of the largest beneficiaries of the compute 
tray design upgrade in the next-gen AI server system, driven by the additional 
chips placed in the tray (for inference processing), as each incremental chip 
will require a lid as well, in addition to the existing AI GPUs and CPUs.
•
Why do we think micro-channel lid can be adopted in 2H26 vs consensus 
of 2H27? First, we believe the chip customer has been facilitating the related 
supply chain to test the micro-channel lid solution in order to realize faster and 
more meaningful spec upgrades. Based on our industry check, the current 
testing/qualification of micro-channel lid adoption at chip level has been 
smooth so far. Second, even if there are lingering supply chain issues before the 
production schedule of the next-gen AI GPU (expected in 3Q26), we believe 
the the customer will still adopt micro-channel lid “during the next AI 
GPU cycle in 2027” as soon as the supply chain issues are resolved (even 
after a few months of mass production already). This is also why we model 
~1mn units of micro-channel lid shipment in 2026, which is relatively 
conservative vs the total expected volume of 2.5-3mn units for next-gen AI 
GPU in 2026. Some investors may pushback stating that customers are likely 
to switch designs back to the existing solution if there are still issues before 
their MP schedule (e.g. the change of board design just a few months before MP 
of this GPU customer’s AI server system), which may cause delay in micro-
channel adoption. However, we believe the AI GPU customer holds a much 
higher conviction to adopt micro-channel lid this time, as the adoption will 
directly impact the “chip-level” performance of its AI GPU (vs. board-
level/system-level design changes previously), hence we maintain a more 
positive view on the micro-channel adoption schedule vs. the Street’s current 
expectations.

Investment Thesis
Jentech (OW) is the largest packaging-level cooling component 
maker worldwide, with leading production capabilities across 
heat spreader products (including stiffener and all kinds of lids). 
We expect the company to grow its EPS at an ~80% CAGR from 
2024-2027E, driven by the solid spec upgrade to micro-channel 
lid (MCL) with significant content growth thanks to the greater 
thermal design power (TDP) of AI GPUs & ASICs, along with 
additional heat spreader adoption in next-gen AI server systems. 
In addition, the company is reinforcing its product portfolio with 
new offerings in cold plate and CPU server sockets for its chip 
customers. We believe Jentech's technology leadership in the 
structural cooling upgrade trend and its new TAM expansion 
will continue to support its superior earnings power in the long 
term. Hence, Jentech is our top pick in the liquid cooling space. 
Valuation

with the company’s 5-year average P/E.

•
Why would the AI GPU customer pull-in its schedule of micro-channel lid adoption 
to 2H26, if cold plate can still solve the heat of its next-gen chip? In our view, the 
breakthrough of cooling component could increase the TDP (Thermal Design Power) / 
the performance of AI server chips significantly. We sense that it is positive for the value 
chain players in the accelerating spec competition race (as most of the peers are trying to 
have meaningful spec migration in their next-gen chips). Hence, although we understand 
that the cold plate enhancement could meet the chip TDP of more than 2000W for the AI 
chips in 2026, we believe this magnitude of upgrade is not meaningful enough for the 
leading AI chip customer. We believe AI GPU would adopt micro-channel lid as soon as 
possible once this new solution is ready for mass production scale, as this cooling 
component evolution could fulfill customers’ request to reach 5000+W in the foreseeable 
future. This upgrade could assure the leading AI chip customer to widen its spec gap vs 
peers.  
•

2025E/26E/27E EPS at NT$37/NT$60/NT$135. Our Dec-26 PT remains at NT$3,650, 
based on an unchanged 27x 2027E P/E, in line with the company’s 5-year average P/E.

Earnings revisions: We factor in 3Q revenues and ﬁne tune our earnings estimates. 
2023E revenue and earnings are revised by -1%/-3% on weaker shipments of general 
servers. 2024-25E earnings are largely unchanged. Our 12-m target price remains 
NT$282. 
 
Quanta is an ODM company focusing on the design and manufacturing of PCs, tablets, 
consumer electronics, servers, etc. We are Buy-rated on Quanta and expect earnings to 
grow in 2024E-25E, driven by 1) PC market recovery in 2024E on consumer PC 
restocking and commercial PC Win 11 upgrade cycle, 2) growing AI server demand from 
Quanta’s CSP customers, and 3) general server demand recovery. We expect 
fast-growing AI servers to contribute to 27%/39%/46% of Quanta’s revenue in 
2023E-25E. We think the Street is underestimating Quanta’s AI server growth potential, 
as the market is concerned with potential competition. Meanwhile, we see Quanta 
maintaining market share in AI servers among cloud customers. We see P/E valuation as 
attractive at the current level compared to its peers given its strong earnings growth in 
2024-25E. Catalysts for further upside/downside would be its customers’ demand on AI 
server and general server/PC demand outlook.

GS Factor Proﬁle 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Proﬁle provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our coverage universe) and its 
sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial 
Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for speciﬁc metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the ﬁscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for ﬁnancial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for ﬁnancial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher ﬁnancial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for ﬁnancial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the ﬁscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the ﬁscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Proﬁle, please contact your GS representative.

announced.

grow in 2026. Investors are also concerned that Marvell’s ASIC growth in
2026 and 2027 could be at the expense of Alchip.
The concern around Marvell's competition for AWS XPU business lingers: While 
we understand investors' concerns, in Joe’s report, he indicated, “In CY26 we think 
that the 20% growth is realistic, and comes mostly from XPU attach opportunities, 
with (per management) minimal contribution from the next big ASIC opportunity”. 
We suggest building positions on dips given Alchip's potential 2026 revenue  upside 
from Trainium3 and its higher revenue content in the Trainium4 product cycle. 
What about Trainium3 news at re:Invent or from the AWS announcement? We 
believe Alchip remains the only true design service provider for Trainium3 because it 
finished the computing die and CoWoS-R circuit designs in July. Some investors have 
asked whether the potential 3nm wafer supply from Broadcom and Marvell for 
Trainium will one day turn into real business for Trainium4 and negatively affect 
Alchip. We think differently and expect the stock to re-rate once Alchip’s earnings 
grow with AWS’s Trainium4 demand during 2027-29. We reiterate our Tranium3

on any correction arising from concerns about Broadcom/Marvell competition in 
Trainium projects –  the competition looks overstated, or the impact on Alchip is 
almost zero.  We reiterate our OW rating on Alchip;  at 20x our 2026e EPS we find 
the stock attractive. Please see inside and Joe Moore’s Astera Labs report for key

FY2Q26 Results 
 Positive implications for Bizlink from Credo's strong FY2Q26 
results, upbeat FY3Q26/FY26 guidance,  and comments on its 
interconnect solutions
FY2Q26 (ended October 2025) results:
• Credo (CRDO.US, not covered) reported  revenue of US$268mn (+20% QoQ/
+272% YoY), exceeding the high-end of its guidance at US$230-240mn.
• Non-GAAP GM was 67.7% (+0.1ppt QoQ; guidance 64-66%) and net profit
was US$128mn (+30% QoQ/+943% YoY).
• Four  customers each contributed more than 10% of its revenue in FY2Q26,
i.e., 42%, 24%, 16%, and 11%, respectively.
FY3Q26 and FY26 outlook:
• Credo guided FY3Q26  revenue to be US$335-345mn (+27% QoQ/+152% YoY
at the mid-point, above consensus at US$248mn),  non-GAAP GM at 64-66%
(vs. consensus at 64.9%) and opex at US$68-72mn, leading to revenue
growth of more than 170%, non-GAAP opex growth  of more than 50%, and
non-GAAP NPM at ~45% for FY26.
• Management expects to see four hyperscaler customers above the 10%
revenue contribution threshold in FY26, with a fifth starting to contribute
initial revenues in FY2Q26 and  a skew toward FY2H26.
• It said it is on track for PCIE AEC design wins in FY26 and meaningful
production revenue in FY27.
• On top of strong growth from AECs (Active Electrical Cables), Credo sees
ALCs (Active LED Cables) being one of the next growth drivers in the coming
years. It targets  first product sampling in FY27 and initial revenue ramp in
FY28. It expects TAM for ALC to be at least twice as large as that for AEC, as
the former can deliver the same reliability and power profile up to 30 meters
of transmission distance.
Read-across:
• We see positive implications for Bizlink from Credo's continuous ramp of
AEC in scale-out networks now, and scale-up networks in the near future, as
well as ALCs in the longer term,
• We stay constructive on Bizlink as we think it will continue to benefit from
volume and dollar content growth from data/power interconnects, as well as
the transition into the subsystem assembly for the semi cap equipment
business (see our report).

最大客戶網通機櫃訂單除由美國擴展至歐亞，產品更延伸至AI 機櫃，
加上Tier 2 CSP AI 伺服器出貨擴增，25~26 年營收維持70%增幅。 
3. 
神達全力擴產支應網通及AI 機櫃強勁成長，且業外豐富轉投資，每年

重點更新 
受惠客戶需求強勁，2Q25 小幅缺料下營運仍創歷史新高  
2Q25 營收266.2 億元，YoY+103%，毛利率10.72%，主要受台幣升值影
響，然營業利益已連續五個季度創下新高，顯示本業獲利明顯優化。3Q25 匯
率升值幅度有限，雖礙於產能滿載，營收估小幅季增2%，然預期營益率將有
所改善至5.4%，營業利益YoY+160%，EPS 1.33 元，4Q25 竹南廠挹注，
營收季增幅擴大至雙位數，今、明年EPS 將跳升至5、8.3 元水準。 
高速成長期才剛開始，神雲營益率由去年1.3%至1H25 大幅跳升至近6% 
神達本業結構明顯改善，2024 年本業轉虧為盈，主要即受惠最大客戶訂單貢
獻，並將擴產因應客戶需求，3Q25 竹南廠將開出網通機櫃產能，服務大客戶

Concentrix 及神基等，穩定的股利配發即可支撐每年EPS 1.5 元貢獻。 
網通機櫃及液冷機櫃為未來數年雙動能 
神達擴廠除因應大客戶網通機櫃需求，近期新增四廠主要將生產網通及液冷
機櫃，顯示AI 伺服器佔比可望逐步攀升，此外，公司與AMD 合作多年，預
期將切入下一代MI 400 系列，估2026 年AI 伺服器成長可望翻倍，網通機
櫃維持高雙位數成長。今年資本支出將年增，主要用於添購製造設備，資金
需求部分，神達將以銀行借款及營運現金流入支應產能擴充因應，且廠區大
多為租用，資本支出規模較同業小，預期短期無增資需求。

此外，神達控股旗下有眾多轉投資，在美國上市公司新聚思TD Synnex (NYSE:SNX) 以及Concentrix 
(NASDAQ:CNXC)獲利穩定，並持有台灣上市公司聯強(2347 TT)、神基(3005 TT)、偉訓(3032 TT)、聯成(1313 TT)

為滿足訂單需求，神達3Q25 竹南廠將開出網通機櫃產能，由原本服務美國地區，額外服務最大客戶歐、亞地區需

轉投資，穩定的股利配發即可支撐每年約EPS 1.5 元貢獻，今、明年EPS 將跳升至5、8.1 元水準。相較於其他伺服

大型CSP 資料中心通常約配置1,500~2,000 個伺服器機櫃，雖伺服器機櫃中配置交換器於機櫃頂端，然大型資料
中心通常會在額外於資料中心設置網通機櫃以利管理網路，過往在通用伺服器為主體的資料中心，伺服器機櫃搭配
網通機櫃的相對配比較低，推估僅約低至中個位數水準，估一個資料中心若有千個伺服器機櫃，僅需配置數十個網
通機櫃即可因應高速網路傳輸。然在AI 浪潮崛起後，AI 伺服器資料中心呈現高密度的配置，預期高階AI 伺服器搭
配網通機櫃的比重將拉升數倍，以反映AI 伺服器更高密度的網路需求。

終端需求回溫、科技巨頭擴增資本支出，製造業景氣有望保持穩健

短期AI需求持續、產業旺季及客戶庫存回補等因素帶動下，研判至2025年底製造業PMI維持在景氣榮枯線50以上。
中長期來看，全球終端需求逐步回溫，科技巨頭持續擴增資本支出，製造業景氣有望保持穩健。
出口再創新高，2025年經濟成長率上修

出口市場結構轉變，美國取代中國成為最大出口國。其中，10月對美出口年增1.4倍，佔總出口比重攀升至34.2%，
穩居第一大出口市場，顯示台灣供應鏈重心已經與美國為首的AI科技生態系緊密結合。

展望未來，第四季出口規模有望超越第三季，且2025年全年累計出口金額將突破6,000億美元。因此，我們將
2025年台灣經濟成長率上修至6.4%。

與時間

期。

軟體生態
極度成熟(NVIDIA CUDA)：擁有龐大的開發
者社區、豐富的工具和高度優化的程式庫。
不成熟/封閉：通常有自己的專有軟體棧，
開發者需學習新的工具，生態系相對封閉且
缺乏通用性。

AMD Instinct MI 系列。
Google TPU (Tensor Processing Unit, 張量處理
單元),

關注中國需求 
 
1. 
中、長期市場需求變化仍需關注中國。中國增發國債刺激經濟增
長，顯示其救經濟的決心。若能加強基礎設施建設，將拉動長期散
裝需求。 
2. 
中國穀物進口部分由澳洲轉向南美，運程延遠，有助運費拉高。因
應減碳要求，中國大陸規劃將粗鋼產量壓減。為實現碳達峰和碳中
和，已連續進行粗鋼減產，這一目標尚未最終確定。此為潛在不利
因素。 
3. 
印度經濟發展用煤增加，吸納部分運力。 
 
 
 
產業趨勢 
 
1. 
此前中國經濟疲弱，基礎工業產能供過於求，中國增發國債刺激經
濟增長，成效不佳。現今推出人民幣1.2兆元的雅魯藏布江下游水
電工程（雅下工程），顯示其救經濟的決心。若能加強基礎設施建
設，將拉動長期散裝需求。 
2. 
其他影響運價有以下幾項：全球原物料需求持平或略增、新船訂單
佔比偏低、國際環保法規加速拆船、乾散貨延噸哩逐年成長。總體
經濟面因素則有：季節性氣候影響、美國維持高利率、大陸房市嚴
峻、運力中期恐呈過剩等因素。 
3. 
因地緣政治，中國戰略上擴大在西非投資鋁礬土礦區。預計今、明
年開採量增加回銷大陸的運輸需求，將可拉升乾散貨延噸哩增加。
此外中國大陸發展AI 需電，電力行業有近100GW燃煤電廠容量開
工建置，達近10年新高。原暫停的3.3GW工程也已復工，帶動電
煤為主的煤炭進口創歷史新高，散裝航運運煤運價有撐。 
4. 
散裝船新船交船量，扣除不符合環保必須拆除的舊船，散裝船的整
體供給可能出現低度成長。過去幾年因為造船廠塢期滿檔，貨櫃輪
排擠散裝船訂新船困難，造成今年散裝船新交船的運力低，有助於
推升散裝船舶運價。

一、營運與財務概況 
1. 
3Q25 毛利率67%。但在疫情紅利過後，營運還是持續有阻
力，目前是虧損狀態。而虧損原因也有為了第二成長動能所
進行的戰略性研發投入。 
2. 
區域別營收：以外銷為主，過往(2018)東南亞32%、中國30%
為兩大主要市場。而近年為避免與低價產品競爭，營運重心
已從中國策略性轉移至東南亞，3Q25 東南亞市場佔比已提
升至54%。 
二、產品與業務結構 
1. 
核心優勢：獨創iiPCR 技術、提供萃取→擴增→判讀的一站
式方案，並具備跨領域整合能力(分子生物/光機電/軟體/精
密製造)，及擁有國際認證。 
2. 
產品組合：水產養殖(佔營收45%)、畜產(30%多)、伴侶動
物(10%多)、IVD 人用和其他。 
3. 
水產養殖為核心業務預期穩定成長，畜產是重點發展業務
(主要東南亞市場)，伴侶動物是新興成長動能。 
4. 
第一曲線深化(2025-2026 短期策略)：聚焦東南亞，鎖定豬
隻、禽類、水產養殖三大產業，提供整合性解決方案。 
5. 
核心機台：POCKIT Central 自動化核酸分析儀，及手持式
POCKIT Micro 系列。 
三、第二成長曲線啟動(NGS 建庫市場與SATLite) 
1. 
過去10 年，定序成本快速下降，但建庫成本變化不大。建
庫成為定序流程中的瓶頸。 
2. 
市場困境：手動建庫耗時費力，需4~8 小時高度集中操作，
且易於出錯、重複性差。而現有自動化，主流設備設計用於
8~96 樣本，導致少量樣本必須湊批才能符合成本效益，犧
牲了時效性。 
3. 
解決方案：SATLite 自動化建庫系統 
定位：鎖定「低通量、即時反應」需求，是為所有實驗室提
供即時結果的快速反應平台。專為1~4 個樣本設計，重量約 
25 公斤左右。

1. 伺服器/資料中心應用方面，GB300 AI伺服器機櫃已於近期放量出
貨，GB300機櫃的Switch Tray之水冷板、快接頭用量較GB200機櫃
有所提升，將挹注公司未來營收成長動能。 
2. 子公司富世達YT3Q25占奇鋐營收9.2%，富世達除供應摺疊手機軸
承，也切入水冷快接頭等AI伺服器零組件應用，表現同樣出色，10
月營收13.1億元，YoY 43.4%，續創單月新高。 
3. 3C應用方面，手機VC部分，今年占整體營收個位數百分比，預期明
年營收占比將提升。  
4. 奇鋐將維持在 NVIDIA 與 ASIC 兩大供應鏈的核心角色，並透過水冷
分歧管 (Manifold) 產品線的份額從明年起顯著擴大至 5-10%，創造
出第二個重要的營收成長動能。Rubin有望導入MCCP成為明年新一
代Vera Rubin散熱解決方案，公司目前協同客戶開發中，看好公司
明年營收及獲利表現將持續向上。 
 
 
 
未來成長動能 
 
1. AI伺服器應用方面(GPU占7成；ASIC占2~3成)，公司看好明年整體
水冷散熱需求強勁，同時也看好ASIC的發展，將是公司未來成長的
一大動能。公司目前已和各大CSP客戶合作這一代及下一代ASIC專
案，同時也與NVIDIA、AMD保持密切合作，目前的ASIC仍以氣冷
方案為主，不過由於目前水冷版本仍在測試中，僅少部分的ASIC採
用水冷散熱。若後續水冷良率提升，則水冷滲透率將進一步提高。
我們預期ASIC AI伺服器未來水冷滲透率將會持續上升。 
2. 我們預估2H26 ASIC有多位客戶新世代水冷板放量，同時公司有望
切入新CSP ASIC水冷板供應。機櫃需求強勁跟降噪機櫃新產品線是
明年另一成長動能。 
3. ASIC 散熱方案由氣冷轉向液冷:目前大多數 ASIC 晶片功耗尚未超過 
1,000W，因此仍主要採用傳統氣冷方案，僅有 AWS Trainium 2.5 
和 Meta MTIA 2 等少數產品開始試行水冷散熱。然而隨著新的資料
中心逐步完成水冷基礎設施的建置，以及未來更高功率晶片的量
產，ASIC 伺服器的水冷滲透率預計將在 2026 年大幅提高。 
4. Trainium 專案詳情： 原本 Trainium 2 採用均熱板 (VC) 氣冷散熱。
從 2025 年第四季量產的 Trainium 2.5 開始，部分機型將導入水冷
散熱，且設計上分為 Compute Tray 和 Switch Tray，每個晶片都將
有獨立的水冷板，並採用 UQD (水冷轉接頭) 進行連接，其採用數量
將明顯高於 GB200/GB300 平台。 
5. 初期挑戰與未來趨勢：雖然 Trainium 3 初期水冷滲透率預計在 20% 
至 30% 之間，但長期來看，對於 Google TPU V6、Meta MTIA 2、
Microsoft Maia 2 和 AWS Trainium 3 等高功率 ASIC 而言，液冷散
熱將成為不可或缺的主流散熱選項。

GS Factor Proﬁle 
The Goldman Sachs Factor Proﬁle provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our coverage universe) and its 
sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial 
Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for speciﬁc metrics for each stock. The 
normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may 
vary depending on the ﬁscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: 
Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for ﬁnancial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a 
higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for ﬁnancial 
stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher ﬁnancial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, 
price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for ﬁnancial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile 
indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns 
percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). 
Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the ﬁscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs 
for the ﬁscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). 
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Proﬁle, please contact your GS representative.  
M&A Rank 
Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary 
across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring 
companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 
representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard 
departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not 
factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

Smoother transition
Expect better-than-feared 4Q25 and promising 2026 outlook
We forecast Wiwynn’s September sales to be NT$85.0bn (-11% MoM, +146% YoY) 
thanks to stronger-than-expected shipments of racks for AWS ASICs. While the 
market has been concerned about the AWS ASIC transition period starting from 
4Q25, we believe robust demand for CSP clients’ regular servers and the ramp-up
for Oracle’s GPU rack demand could mitigate this. We expect Wiwynn’s Mexico 
facility to support Oracle’s GPU rack demand, and its upcoming US plant will 
further support AWS ASIC liquid cooling rack manufacturing from 2H26. We lift 
25-27CT EPS by 6-18% and raise our TP from NT$3,600 to NT$4,200. Maintain 
Outperform.
3Q25 preview
Driven by increased cloud Capex, Wiwynn as the major AWS ASIC L10/L11 supplier
has continued to benefit from ASIC demand. With ongoing robust shipments for 
AWS Trainium2, we forecast September sales of NT$85.0bn, -11% MoM, +146% 
YoY, thanks to the robust demand for AWS ASICs, and this will lead to 3Q25CT
revenue of NT$266bn, which is 17% higher than consensus forecasts.
AWS ASIC transition impact could be mitigated
While the market has been concerned about the period of AWS’ ASIC transition 
from Trainium2 to Trainium3, we believe Wiwynn has two strong catalysts to 
mitigate any impact: regular servers and Oracle AI servers. We see continued
strength in CSP regular server demand into 4Q25. And for Oracle’s orders, 
Wiwynn’s Mexico plant could facilitate manufacturing from L10/L11. We expect 
the revenue contribution from Oracle to begin from 4Q25 and reach 5% into 2026
with upside risk.
Stronger 2026 outlook
As new US capacity comes online in end-4Q25/early-1Q26, Wiwynn will complete 
the manufacturing support for key customers’ AI server demand under the current 
uncertain US tariff conditions. Its US plant will focus on production of liquid cooling 
server racks, in line with the trend of ASIC liquid cooling adoption from 4Q25 
onwards. Into 2026, with AWS’ rising ASIC demand for Trainium3 and ongoing order
share wins in GPU racks, we forecast 2026 sales to grow 10% YoY.
Earnings revisions and valuation
We lift 25/26/27CT EPS by 6%/14%/18% to reflect the strong near-term demand 
from AWS Trainium2, higher revenue contribution from AWS Trainium3 and 
Oracle’s GPU server shipments, resulting in a higher TP of NT$4,200 (from 
NT$3,600), still based on 16x 26CT PE. Maintain Outperform.

Investment thesis
Expect it to benefit from strong CSP ASIC server demand in 2025; new server 
platform ramp-ups and accelerating ASIC server shipments. Risk-reward looks 
favourable even if there is no AI contribution from the Middle East.
Catalysts
1) Stronger-than-expected ASIC server demand; 2) faster-than-expected general 
server shipment ramp-up; 3) better-than-expected Middle East contribution.
Valuation details
Our target price is based on a PE valuation methodology as we believe it better 
reflects market expectations for the company’s earnings growth outlook. Our target 
price is based on 16x 2026CT PE, 1sd above the five-year average PE, to factor in 
stronger AI and ASIC server demand despite the removal of the Middle East 
contribution. We believe a 16x PE is justified given its 51% EPS Cagr over 24-27CT.
Investment risks
Risks include 1) a slowdown in CSP clients’ Capex investment, which could lead to 
a more subdued revenue outlook; 2) intensifying competition in datacentre 
hardware that may result in order loss and/or margin pressure; 3) slower-than-
expected ramp-up of new business development, especially in new client and AI 
penetration, that could lead to a more volatile earnings profile; and 4) short supply 
of key components that would impede the schedule for product shipments and the 
revenue outlook.
